cases.title: Chest Pain — Suspected STEMI
cases.presentation: A 58-year-old man presents with 45 minutes of crushing central chest pain, diaphoresis and nausea. History: hypertension and smoking. He is awake, pale and uncomfortable.
objectives: Obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG rapidly
Initiate appropriate monitored care and reperfusion pathway

references.title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
references.note: Verify local STEMI pathway and current full guideline before clinical use

steps.prompt: The patient has just arrived. What are your immediate priorities?

rules.label: Immediate assessment, monitor, IV access
rules.feedback: Assess ABCs, stability, monitor and establish access.

rules.label: 12-lead ECG immediately
rules.feedback: Acquire and interpret a 12-lead ECG promptly.

rules.label: Ask about symptoms, medications and contraindications
rules.feedback: Focused history helps management without delaying urgent ECG.

rules.label: Routine CT scan before ECG
rules.feedback: A routine CT is not the priority for typical suspected ACS.

rules.label: Discharge without assessment
rules.feedback: Unsafe before evaluating potentially life-threatening chest pain.

updates.ecg: ECG is now available: ST elevation in II, III, aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL.

steps.prompt: The ECG shows ST elevation in II, III, aVF and reciprocal depression in I and aVL. Interpret it and state your next priority.

rules.label: Inferior STEMI; activate reperfusion pathway
rules.feedback: Treat as STEMI and activate an appropriate rapid reperfusion pathway.

rules.label: Check right-sided leads if RV involvement suspected
rules.feedback: Right ventricular involvement matters for hemodynamic management.

rules.label: Wait for troponin before activating cath lab
rules.feedback: A diagnostic STEMI ECG should not await troponin before reperfusion activation.

rules.label: Treat as simple reflux and discharge
rules.feedback: Incompatible with the diagnostic ECG.

rules.label: Repeat ECG and obtain serial ECGs
rules.feedback: Useful when clinically indicated, but should not delay reperfusion.

steps.prompt: You have activated the STEMI pathway. What medical measures and safety checks are appropriate while arranging reperfusion?

rules.label: Give chewable aspirin if no contraindication
rules.feedback: Aspirin is a core initial antiplatelet measure when appropriate.

rules.label: Follow protocol for antithrombotics and urgent PCI
rules.feedback: Use guideline- and local-pathway-directed antithrombotics and PCI.

rules.label: Evaluate nitrate contraindications
rules.feedback: Avoid routine nitrates when hypotensive or RV infarction/PDE5 concerns exist.

rules.label: Routine oxygen despite normal saturation
rules.feedback: Routine oxygen is not indicated solely for ACS when saturation is adequate and no hypoxemia.

rules.label: Give thrombolytic despite immediately available PCI without assessment
rules.feedback: Reperfusion selection depends on timely PCI availability, contraindications and protocol.

rules.label: Administer nitrates in hypotension or suspected RV infarction
rules.feedback: May precipitate severe hypotension.

steps.prompt: While awaiting transfer, the patient becomes dizzy and his BP falls. What now?

rules.label: Reassess ABCs and perfusion immediately
rules.feedback: Urgent reassessment and hemodynamic support are needed.

rules.label: Assess for RV infarction and bradyarrhythmia
rules.feedback: Inferior STEMI can involve RV infarction and conduction abnormalities.

rules.label: Escalate to resuscitation team and expedite reperfusion
rules.feedback: Escalate instability and expedite definitive care.

rules.label: Continue nitrates despite hypotension
rules.feedback: Nitrates can worsen hypotension in this setting.

rules.label: Send home because pain improved
rules.feedback: Clinical instability requires urgent management.

steps.prompt: After stabilization and urgent coronary intervention, what disposition and monitoring are appropriate?

rules.label: Admit to monitored cardiac care
rules.feedback: Monitor for recurrent ischemia, arrhythmias and complications.

rules.label: Continue secondary prevention and follow-up
rules.feedback: Plan evidence-based secondary prevention and rehabilitation.

rules.label: Immediate discharge without observation
rules.feedback: Post-STEMI monitoring and ongoing care are required.

cases.title: Acute Severe Asthma
cases.presentation: A 24-year-old woman with asthma arrives struggling to speak full sentences. She has used her rescue inhaler repeatedly with little benefit. No known cardiac disease.
objectives: Assess severity and impending respiratory failure
Initiate inhaled bronchodilator and systemic steroid treatment
Avoid unsafe sedation and delayed reassessment

references.title: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report
references.note: Use latest available report and local acute asthma pathway

steps.prompt: She is using accessory muscles and speaks only in phrases. What do you do immediately?
steps.vitals: BP 132/82 · HR 126 · RR 32 · SpO₂ 89% on room air

rules.label: ABCDE, severity assessment and monitoring
rules.feedback: Assess airway, breathing, work of breathing and mental status.

rules.label: Give controlled supplemental oxygen
rules.feedback: Treat hypoxemia and titrate to the recommended target range.

rules.label: Inhaled short-acting beta agonist promptly
rules.feedback: Rapid-acting inhaled bronchodilator therapy is essential.

rules.label: Systemic corticosteroid early
rules.feedback: Early systemic corticosteroids reduce relapse and admission risk.

rules.label: Sedate to reduce anxiety
rules.feedback: Sedation can worsen respiratory compromise.

rules.label: Discharge immediately
rules.feedback: Severe hypoxemia and distress require urgent treatment.

steps.prompt: After initial treatment, she remains tachypneic and hypoxemic. What next?
steps.vitals: BP 128/78 · HR 124 · RR 30 · SpO₂ 91% with oxygen

rules.label: Repeat bronchodilator and add inhaled ipratropium
rules.feedback: Repeated SABA plus ipratropium is appropriate in severe exacerbation.

rules.label: Consider IV magnesium sulfate in severe poor response
rules.feedback: IV magnesium may be appropriate for severe attacks not responding to initial therapy.

rules.label: Reassess frequently and escalate
rules.feedback: Repeat assessments and early escalation are essential.

rules.label: Routine antibiotics without infection evidence
rules.feedback: Antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated asthma exacerbation.

rules.label: Delay treatment for chest X-ray
rules.feedback: Do not delay treatment for nonessential imaging.

steps.prompt: She becomes drowsy and chest auscultation is now very quiet. What is your interpretation and response?
steps.vitals: BP 100/64 · HR 138 · RR 12 · SpO₂ 86% despite oxygen

rules.label: Recognize impending respiratory failure
rules.feedback: Drowsiness, reduced effort and a quiet chest are danger signs.

rules.label: Call critical care and prepare airway support
rules.feedback: Urgent experienced airway/critical-care support is needed.

rules.label: Continue monitored bronchodilator treatment
rules.feedback: Continue indicated therapy while preparing escalation.

rules.label: Reassure and leave unmonitored
rules.feedback: May progress to respiratory arrest.

rules.label: Give sedative without airway plan
rules.feedback: Can precipitate respiratory failure.

steps.prompt: Following appropriate advanced support, the patient improves. What do you reassess?
steps.vitals: BP 118/74 · HR 108 · RR 22 · SpO₂ 96% on support

rules.label: Reassess respiratory status and objective response
rules.feedback: Track oxygenation, ventilation, fatigue and response to therapy.

rules.label: Review need for ongoing monitoring and admission
rules.feedback: A near-fatal episode requires monitored disposition.

rules.label: Discharge without review
rules.feedback: Inappropriate after impending respiratory failure.

cases.title: Sudden Collapse — VF Cardiac Arrest
cases.presentation: A 63-year-old patient collapses in the Emergency Department waiting area. He is unresponsive and has no normal breathing. Staff are at the bedside.
objectives: Recognize arrest and start high-quality CPR
Perform timed ACLS cycles and treat reversible causes
Recognize ROSC and begin post-arrest care

references.title: American Heart Association CPR & ECC Guidelines
references.note: Verify current adult cardiac arrest algorithm and local resuscitation policy

steps.prompt: The patient is unresponsive and not breathing normally. What are your first actions?
steps.vitals: Unresponsive · Agonal breathing · No definite pulse within 10 seconds

rules.label: Call for help and activate resuscitation
rules.feedback: Activate the arrest response immediately.

rules.label: Start high-quality chest compressions
rules.feedback: Start CPR immediately and minimize interruptions.

rules.label: Attach defibrillator or AED
rules.feedback: Obtain rhythm analysis and prepare for defibrillation.

rules.label: Prolonged pulse check
rules.feedback: Do not delay CPR with prolonged pulse checks.

rules.label: CT scan before CPR
rules.feedback: Imaging must not delay life-saving resuscitation.

steps.prompt: Monitor shows ventricular fibrillation (VF). What now?

rules.label: Deliver unsynchronized defibrillation
rules.feedback: VF is shockable: defibrillate promptly with device-appropriate energy.

rules.label: Resume CPR immediately after shock
rules.feedback: Resume high-quality CPR immediately after shock.

rules.label: Synchronized cardioversion
rules.feedback: Synchronized cardioversion is not the treatment for pulseless VF.

rules.label: Atropine for VF
rules.feedback: Atropine is not a treatment for VF arrest.

rules.label: Wait for IV access before first shock
rules.feedback: Do not delay defibrillation for vascular access.

steps.prompt: After a shock, VF persists on the next rhythm check. Describe ongoing resuscitation.

rules.label: Continue two-minute CPR cycles and rhythm checks
rules.feedback: Maintain high-quality CPR with brief rhythm checks.

rules.label: Repeat defibrillation for persistent VF
rules.feedback: Shock persistent VF according to ACLS algorithm.

rules.label: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO per ACLS timing
rules.feedback: Adult cardiac arrest epinephrine is 1 mg IV/IO at guideline intervals; timing follows the shockable algorithm.

rules.label: Amiodarone for refractory VF per protocol
rules.feedback: Consider antiarrhythmic therapy for refractory VF per ACLS algorithm.

rules.label: Search reversible causes
rules.feedback: Identify and treat reversible causes.

rules.label: Stop CPR for prolonged discussion
rules.feedback: Prolonged CPR interruptions reduce perfusion.

steps.prompt: A pulse returns and the patient is breathing with assistance. What now?
steps.vitals: BP 94/58 · HR 112 sinus · SpO₂ 93% with assisted ventilation

rules.label: Confirm ROSC and reassess ABCDE
rules.feedback: Confirm circulation and stabilize airway, ventilation and perfusion.

rules.label: Post-arrest ECG and evaluate cause
rules.feedback: Evaluate cause including acute coronary occlusion when suspected.

rules.label: Optimize oxygenation, ventilation and blood pressure
rules.feedback: Avoid hypoxemia, hyperoxemia and hypotension through titrated care.

rules.label: Transfer to critical care
rules.feedback: Ongoing post-arrest care needs monitored critical-care setting.

rules.label: Immediately discharge after ROSC
rules.feedback: Post-cardiac arrest care is essential.
